items.claim: The onset, the marks and the frame all check out, but a byte-true catchword straddles this row's own rear seam undisclosed, and one signal key names a divine-title class the cited verse's bytes do not carry.
items.evidence: Verified first. The opener כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.66.1-Isa.66.1) re-collates at BYTE tier and stands verse-initial as tokens 1-3; the frame owner is inside the quoted run, so the messenger formula here is the divine frame, not the royal-messenger use confined to the narrative chapters, and MT 66 is outside both offset zones (identity numbering, no dual-cite owed). Against the single-witness paragraph-mark inventory (MT keys) the two cited breaks are real and correctly typed SAMEKH, at MT 65:25 and MT 66:4; those are the chapter's front-seam and first internal marks, no PE stands anywhere in MT 66 (inventory: 3 SAMEKH segs and 0 PE segs in this chapter, at MT 66:4, 66:9 and 66:11; nearest PE is MT 65:12), and MT 66:1-4 carries no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note, so the span-relevant disclosure set is complete. First defect. MT 66:2 closes וְחָרֵ֖ד עַל דְּבָרִֽי (oshb:Isa.66.2-Isa.66.2) and MT 66:5 opens שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה הַחֲרֵדִ֖ים אֶל דְּבָר֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.66.5-Isa.66.5): the trembler-plus-word pairing sits on both sides of this row's own 66:4|66:5 seam and defines the next unit's addressees from inside this one. The trembling root stands in 7 verses book-wide (sweep: 7 verses at MT 10:29, 19:16, 21:4, 32:11, 41:5, 66:2, 66:5, skeleton tier) and MT 66:2/66:5 are its only adjacent pair and its only sites in this chapter. A byte-true device across a row's own seam argues continuity against the cut unless disclosed, and nothing in the row discloses it; the cut itself still stands on the verse-initial imperative at MT 66:5 plus the marked break. Second defect. The second signal key names a divine-title class, but MT 66:1's הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם כִּסְאִ֔י וְהָאָ֖רֶץ הֲדֹ֣ם רַגְלָ֑י is two verbless predications; no title form stands in the verse, and its only title-class token is the tetragrammaton already carried by the frame key, so the key asserts a signal the bytes do not supply at that site. Third defect. The unit's characterization leans on the rendering's supplied comparative, “is as” (web:Isa.66.3-Isa.66.3), where the Hebrew juxtaposes bare participles, שׁוֹחֵ֨ט הַשּׁ֜וֹר מַכֵּה אִ֗ישׁ (oshb:Isa.66.3-Isa.66.3), with no comparative particle - a construal the bytes leave open.

items.claim: The rival cut at 66:5|66:6 is rejected on an absence claim the bytes contradict: MT 66:6 is a verse-initial threefold herald-voice verse with a change of grammatical person.
items.evidence: Verified first. שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.66.5-Isa.66.5) re-collates at BYTE tier and is verse-initial; the masculine-plural imperative form is carried by the pointed bytes and by both witnesses' renderings, so the onset claim holds. Marks check out against the single-witness inventory: SAMEKH at MT 66:4 and MT 66:9, correctly typed, with no PE, no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note anywhere in MT 66:5-9, so the span's disclosure set is complete. The close is stronger than the row says: MT 66:9 ends verse-finally with the Elohim variant of the postpositive signature, אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.66.9-Isa.66.9), a genuine closure signal the row quotes in translation but never names as such. Defect. The row's rival disclosure rejects a 66:5|66:6 cut on the ground that no addressee or frame shift divides them; that is the one thing the bytes contest there. MT 66:6 opens ק֤וֹל שָׁאוֹן֙ מֵעִ֔יר (oshb:Isa.66.6-Isa.66.6) and stacks three herald-voice tokens in a single verse, and a verse-initial herald-voice opener occurs in exactly 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses at MT 13:4, 40:3, 40:6, 52:8, 66:6, skeleton tier) - the same class as the herald openers at MT 40:3 and 40:6, which are treated as tier-1 scene-shift signals where explicit in the bytes. The verse also drops the second-person address that governs MT 66:5 (הַחֲרֵדִ֖ים אֶל דְּבָר֑וֹ, וְנִרְאֶ֥ה בְשִׂמְחַתְכֶ֖ם) for third-person report, so both halves of the asserted absence fail. The boundary at 66:5 and 66:9 is not itself contested; the rival's stated ground is.

items.claim: The retention argument for this two-verse unit mislabels its rear-seam signal as an imperative onset, and the suckle catchword crossing that same seam is disclosed only in translation.
items.evidence: Verified first. שִׂמְח֧וּ אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם (oshb:Isa.66.10-Isa.66.10) re-collates at BYTE tier, is verse-initial, and is one of three imperatives in the verse (שִׂמְח֧וּ אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם, וְגִ֥ילוּ, שִׂ֤ישׂוּ), so the onset claim is byte-true. The addressee contrast is byte-true as well: כָּל אֹהֲבֶ֑יהָ and כָּל הַמִּֽתְאַבְּלִ֖ים עָלֶֽיהָ here against הַחֲרֵדִ֖ים אֶל דְּבָר֑וֹ (oshb:Isa.66.5-Isa.66.5) in the preceding unit. Marks check out: SAMEKH at MT 66:9 and MT 66:11, correctly typed, no PE, and no paseq seg or ketiv/qere note in MT 66:10-11. First defect. The retention note claims tier-1 imperative onsets on either side of the unit. MT 66:12 opens כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.66.12-Isa.66.12) and carries no imperative among its 20 tokens, on the pointed bytes and on both witnesses' renderings; its onset is a messenger frame, exactly as the row's own boundary prose says elsewhere. The form-class label contradicts the row's own reading and cannot be sustained from the bytes on the rear side. Second defect. תִּֽינְקוּ֙ (oshb:Isa.66.11-Isa.66.11) and וִֽינַקְתֶּ֑ם (oshb:Isa.66.12-Isa.66.12) put the same suckle root on both sides of the row's rear seam; the attested family sites are MT 60:16, 66:11 and 66:12 (a bare three-letter substring sweep returns 4 verses, one of which - MT 29:1 - belongs to a different root and is the short-token trap, so the object here is the suckle family at 3 verses, skeleton tier). The row discloses this only as English nursing-and-comfort imagery, without the Hebrew form or a tier label, where a boundary-relevant cohesion claim owes the pointed form and its tier. The boundary itself stands on the messenger frame at MT 66:12.

items.claim: Onset, close, rival handling and every disclosure object in MT 66:12-14 hold against the bytes and the single-witness inventories.
items.evidence: The opener כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.66.12-Isa.66.12) re-collates at BYTE tier and is verse-initial; the frame owner stands inside the quoted run, and this is a divine frame, not one of the royal-messenger uses confined to the narrative chapters. The rear-seam onset survives the byte test rather than resting on register alone: the opener כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה (oshb:Isa.66.15-Isa.66.15) is verse-initial in exactly 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses at MT 3:1, 26:21, 60:2, 66:15, skeleton tier), three of them announcing a divine advent, so MT 66:15 instantiates a recurring announcement opener even though its particle also links back. The rival - reading the close of MT 66:14 as the judgment onset - is answered correctly from the bytes: וְנוֹדְעָ֤ה יַד יְהוָה֙ אֶת עֲבָדָ֔יו וְזָעַ֖ם אֶת אֹיְבָֽיו (oshb:Isa.66.14-Isa.66.14) is third-person report with no frame, vocative or imperative. Disclosure objects check out: SAMEKH at MT 66:11 is present and correctly typed against the single-witness inventory, the paseq at MT 66:12 is 1 seg and is cited count-only with no intra-verse position asserted, no mark falls at MT 66:12-14 (stated correctly), and no ketiv/qere note stands in the span, so span-relevant symmetry is complete. One non-blocking reservation: the paseq is carried in the reference list but never engaged in the row's prose.

items.claim: Both seams, the postpositive close and the ketiv/qere handling hold against the bytes; the only soft spot is an illustrative gloss that outruns the Hebrew.
items.evidence: The opener כִּֽי הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בָּאֵ֣שׁ יָב֔וֹא (oshb:Isa.66.15-Isa.66.15) re-collates at BYTE tier and is verse-initial, and its two-word opener is one of only 4 verse-initial instances book-wide (sweep: 4 verses at MT 3:1, 26:21, 60:2, 66:15, skeleton tier). The close is genuinely what the row calls it: נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.66.17-Isa.66.17) re-collates at BYTE tier and is verse-final - the contiguous postpositive pair stands in 19 verses book-wide and is verse-final in only 6 (sweep: 6 verses at MT 14:22, 37:34, 54:17, 55:8, 59:20, 66:17, skeleton tier) - and its final token carries no dividing accent, only a meteg, so the position claim is byte-checked, not assumed. Ketiv/qere handling is right: the single-witness inventory records exactly 1 note at MT 66:17, the row discloses it, takes no position on the reading, and performs no counting or slicing inside that verse. Marks are stated correctly: no PE and no SAMEKH at MT 66:14 or anywhere in MT 66:15-17, and no paseq seg in the span, so the boundaries do rest on tier-1 signals alone as claimed. One non-blocking reservation: the rear-seam gloss quotes “For I know” (web:Isa.66.18-Isa.66.18), where MT 66:18 opens וְאָנֹכִ֗י מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם֙ וּמַחְשְׁבֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם בָּאָ֕ה (oshb:Isa.66.18-Isa.66.18) with no causal particle and no verb of knowing, and the pronoun is prefixed with a connective; the stated ground - a first-person emphatic pivot into a new subject - is nonetheless byte-true, so the seam is not contested.

items.claim: The closing warrant is byte-false - the postpositive signature at MT 66:22 stands mid-verse at the major divider, while the verse-final signature the row describes sits at MT 66:21 inside the span, undisclosed and against the row's own rival ground.
items.evidence: Every quoted run re-collates at BYTE tier, so the defects are positional and count-level, not copy-degradation. First defect. נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.66.22-Isa.66.22) is token 12 of 17: its divine-name token carries the verse's major dividing accent and four words follow it, כֵּ֛ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם וְשִׁמְכֶֽם, completing the comparison opened by כִּ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר. It is a parenthesis inside that construction, not a seal on the unit; the rendering sets it mid-sentence too (“says Yahweh”, web:Isa.66.22-Isa.66.22), so both witnesses agree against the row. Contrast MT 66:17, where the same pair is verse-final with no dividing accent. Second defect. MT 66:21 ends אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.66.21-Isa.66.21), verse-finally. The contiguous speech-signature pair stands in 53 verses book-wide but is verse-final in only 5 (sweep: 5 verses at MT 39:6, 54:1, 65:25, 66:21, 66:23, skeleton tier); two of those five are in this chapter, and MT 66:21's falls inside this row's span. That is an undisclosed closure-class signal of exactly the class the row invokes, and it contests the row's rival ground: MT 66:21 is not a further clause of a running sentence-sequence but a complete clause, וְגַם מֵהֶ֥ם אֶקַּ֛ח לַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים לַלְוִיִּ֖ם, terminated by that signature, with MT 66:22 opening a fresh comparative construction. Third defect. The recurrence tier is overstated. MT 65:17 reads שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה (oshb:Isa.65.17-Isa.65.17) indefinite, MT 66:22 הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם הַ֠חֳדָשִׁים וְהָאָ֨רֶץ הַחֲדָשָׁ֜ה definite; each four-token string occurs in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse each, skeleton tier) and even their two-token pairs do not cross. The link is a lexical collocation with different determination, not the skeleton-tier recurrence the row labels it. Fourth defect, count-level. The paseq disclosure describes MT 66:20 as a single count-layer segment; the single-witness inventory records 2 segs there (1 at MT 66:19). Verified correct: no PE or SAMEKH falls in MT 66:18-22 and none is claimed, and no ketiv/qere note stands in the span.

items.claim: The couplet's internal turn falls on one of the book's five verse-final speech signatures, which the row neither quotes nor weighs while resting the held coda question on external scholarship instead of the bytes.
items.evidence: Verified first: both quoted runs re-collate at BYTE tier, MT 66 is outside both offset zones, and the mark statements are right - no PE or SAMEKH stands in MT 66:23-24 or at MT 66:22, the chapter's only marks being SAMEKH at MT 66:4, 66:9 and 66:11, with no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note in the closing span. First defect. MT 66:23 ends אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Isa.66.23-Isa.66.23), verse-finally; the contiguous speech-signature pair is verse-final in only 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses at MT 39:6, 54:1, 65:25, 66:21, 66:23, skeleton tier). It falls exactly at the turn the row identifies between universal worship and the closing image, and the row's own rendering quote stops one clause short of it (“says Yahweh”, web:Isa.66.23-Isa.66.23, is the clause left out). Because the row's terminal-unit decision rests on that internal turn, this is the byte evidence bearing most directly on the held coda-versus-conclusion question, and it is neither cited nor weighed. Second defect. The byte-level tie that argues the other way - for holding the couplet together - is also uncited: יָב֧וֹא כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר at MT 66:23 and לְכָל בָּשָֽׂר verse-final at MT 66:24 (oshb:Isa.66.24-Isa.66.24), with the chapter's third site at MT 66:16 (sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, skeleton tier). The held item is left with no byte evidence on either side. Third defect. The front seam rests on a content distinction between recurring and one-time reference, and MT 66:23 opens וְהָיָ֗ה - a connective-prefixed continuation, not a frame, vocative, imperative or superscription onset - so no tier-1 signal is offered for the 66:22|66:23 cut; and the rival disclosure grounds the retention on an unresolved scholarly question, where extra-textual scholarly debate is metadata and carries no boundary authority in this book. Holding the question is right; grounding it there is not.
